clue.text: Including everything at school

definitions.meaning: a British state secondary school taking pupils of all abilities

explanation.surface: Someone describes a school curriculum that covers every subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means all-inclusive, and in Britain it also names the non-selective state secondary school.

clue.text: Old rum I put into another container

indicators.note: the letters are put into another arrangement, so these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone decants old rum into a different vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into another' seems to describe pouring liquor between vessels; it tells you to rearrange OLD RUM I.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum for oil is a large metal vessel for storing liquids.

clue.text: Suffering from the effects of French bread?

definitions.meaning: the French word for a loaf

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after eating a baguette.
explanation.definitionFit: The English word means hurt, while the identical French word means a loaf.

clue.text: The way 'stretches' becomes 'seek'

parts.note: read the entry as instructions: the letters of the first word, with 'out' as an anagram signal, rearrange to give this word

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle about how one word turns into another.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: EKES, put 'out' of order, makes SEEK, which is why the clue says 'stretches' becomes 'seek'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke something out is to make a scant supply last longer, spinning it thinner.

clue.text: Pointed remark about age — prim rejoinder

indicators.note: about signals the words are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A prudish retort to a comment on someone's age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AGE and PRIM; 'rejoinder' only extends the picture of a witty reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, witty, barbed saying.

clue.text: It's added to drink like so, pop!

explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water is a common mixer topped up into whisky or other spirits.

clue.text: A ship's success

definitions.meaning: Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, HMS ..., preserved at Portsmouth

explanation.surface: A remark about a vessel doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: It names Nelson's famous flagship and also means a triumph in battle or contest.

clue.text: There is point to much of their work

definitions.text: There is point to much of their work

parts.words: There is point to much of their work
parts.note: the 'point' is the tip of the toe on which these performers spend much of their working time, en pointe

explanation.definitionFit: Ballerinas dance on the points of their toes, so pointe work is central to the job.

clue.text: Alien nations, we hear

parts.note: the two words said together sound like a single word for falling-outs or estrangement between people

explanation.definitionFit: Spoken aloud, 'alien nations' sounds like 'alienations', a synonym for rifts between former friends.

clue.text: Ever a struggle with team ill

indicators.note: a struggle throws the letters about, so these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sick team has a constant fight on its hands.
explanation.definitionFit: As in an all-time record: the greatest of any period, so ever recorded.

clue.text: Pointers on making Indian desserts

parts.note: IND is a standard abbreviation for Indian or India
ices are frozen sweet courses

explanation.surface: Advice on how to make sweet dishes from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Indexes are pointers, like the index finger or a pointer on a dial; the plural form fits.

clue.text: Learning to look about

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
re is Latin for concerning, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: Education means paying attention to your surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge passed down, a body of learning.

clue.text: How and where to woo a judge?

definitions.meaning: the verb for wooing, and the yard or royal household where wooing went on
the tribunal or bench that sits in judgement

explanation.surface: A lover wonders how and where to romance someone on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To court is to woo, a court is an enclosed space or royal household, and a court of law judges cases.

clue.text: Lout shouting down the rector?

parts.note: to boo is to jeer someone into silence
R is an abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: Someone rudely heckles the parish priest.

explanation.definitionFit: A boor is a rude, coarse person, an oaf.

clue.text: Listen on the doorstep to find mother

definitions.text: Listen on the doorstep to find mother

parts.words: Listen on the doorstep to find mother
parts.note: alludes to the old British music-hall song 'On Mother ... Doorstep', whose title pairs a mother with a doorstep

explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the title of the popular song about a mother's doorstep in Paradise Row.

clue.text: French ice-cream sometimes given to kid

definitions.meaning: the French word for ice or ice cream
describes soft, glossy goatskin leather given a glazed finish

explanation.surface: A treat a child is sometimes allowed from a French vendor.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word means ice cream, and glazed goatskin is known as glacé kid leather.

clue.text: Play that goes down a storm!

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's late drama set on an island

explanation.surface: A theatre production that was a huge success.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Shakespeare's drama about Prospero and also a word for a violent gale.

clue.text: Asian chap with a song in his heart

indicators.note: the second piece goes into the middle of the first, its heart

a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A man from Asia with a tune he holds dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in his heart' puts A LAY into the middle of MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Malay peninsula is a native of South-East Asia.

clue.text: A painter's yarn?

definitions.meaning: a type of quick-drying artist's paint
a synthetic fibre spun for knitting

explanation.surface: An artist tells a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a synthetic paint used by artists and a man-made knitting wool.

clue.text: He'll belittle the dieter

explanation.surface: A critic will mock someone on a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes things smaller, or slims, can be called by this word.

clue.text: One musical work you can say good-bye to

parts.note: taken as written
ta-ta is an informal farewell

explanation.surface: A piece of music so poor you are happy to walk away from it.

clue.text: Ghastly link between Scotsman, sailor and soldiers

clue.text: The high spot for any muezzin

clue.text: Regulatory system on fish numbers

clue.text: Concerning the Scots

taken as written
